findings.reason: naming the owner to extend keeps the zero/one/many policy in one place, so a later change to bundle precedence or machine declaration cannot drift the guard away from the resolution the tests actually exercise.
findings.text: the guard "decides absence from `discover_bundles()` alone" and so re-derives the membership filter (`machine in bundle.machines` over the discovered bundles) that `bundle_for_machine` already owns at packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/machine_map.py:290-292, where the same list comprehension decides the machine→bundle answer; the section does not say why the owner cannot expose the presence question (e.g. the match list, or `bundles_carrying(machine)`), so the test helper becomes a second, unowned copy of the resolution policy

findings.reason: the census of the duplication being consolidated is incomplete, so the author must either fold this fixture into the single owner or say in the section why this stand-in is deliberately separate, before its "defined once" measure can hold.
findings.text: §14 says "the stand-in gets one owner too" and names only `tests/data/test_eddb_local_transport.py:38` and `packages/imas-alambic/tests/test_eddb_local_transport.py:38`, but a third stand-in of the same type survives: `FAKE_WRAPPER` at tests/data/test_eddb_cache.py:63 defines its own `class eddbWrapper` at :73 and is written as `eddb_pwrapper.py` at :221, a local stand-in module on the reader script's path exactly as the pair the section consolidates; §14's done-when then reads "the stand-in wrapper and helpers are defined once", which the third definition makes false

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `tests/jt60sa_bundle.py` hides bundle discovery, the zero/one/many decision, the stated reason and the skip marker behind one machine parameter; the engine `eddb_standin.py` hides the wrapper text and the channels-table writer.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §14 consolidates the EDDB stand-in onto one owner but names only two of the three files that define a stand-in `eddbWrapper` module.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §14 adds only test-support modules (`tests/jt60sa_bundle.py`, `packages/imas-alambic/tests/eddb_standin.py`) and in its own text merges nine guards into one owner and the stand-in wrapper into one owner.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §14 cites the mechanisms it extends (`discover_bundles`/`bundle_for_machine`), the engine-side stand-in file it consolidates onto (`packages/imas-alambic/tests/test_+eddb_local_transport.py`), and settles the load-by-path mechanism with a reason; a shared non-test helper module in `tests/` also matches the repo's own precedent (`tests/distribution_sources.py`, imported by two test modules).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the guard is a thin layer over `discover_bundles` that re-derives the machine→bundle membership predicate `bundle_for_machine` already owns, without saying why that owner cannot expose it.
